content: Official GitHub documentation says a README should explain what a project does, why it is useful, how to get started, where to get help, and who maintains it; a detectable repository license clarifies reuse; GitHub releases package release notes and downloadable binary assets. Developer's Hell v1 should ship a root README with screenshots/GIF, exact Fabric/JDK/install/build instructions and module matrix, a license plus asset provenance/credits, and a tagged release containing the tested JAR and concise known limitations.
